svg.text: Sheet 3 · Pinouts for the parts that are easy to get wrong
5-pin DIN sockets X1-X3 · Same Sky SDS-50J (female, right-angle PCB)
MIDI numbering runs 1-4-2-5-3 around the arc. Pin 2 (centre) = shield. Viewed from the front of a socket, pin 1 is on the RIGHT.
Pin positions taken from the Same Sky SDS-50J mechanical drawing (front view and recommended PCB layout).
key notch at top; yellow 4/5 = loop, blue 2 = shield
TOP view (component side), as on sheet 1
The shell tabs (E) are not used on the breadboard. Never ground the MIDI IN shell or pin 2: the IN side must stay isolated (wiring.md section 2).
Socket pins are on a 2.5/5 mm grid, not 0.1": solder short (~15 cm) solid-core leads, sleeve each joint, label the socket.
From the Omron G5V-2 datasheet, 'Terminal arrangement / internal connections (bottom view)'.
VERIFY against your datasheet and with a meter before fitting.
Rows 0.3" apart: straddles the channel like a DIP-16.
Notch (and pin-1 dot) to the LEFT on board 2 (rows 26-28).
Legs spread to 0.1": E e9, B e10, C e11.
E = GND, B ← 1k ← GP2, C = COIL-.
top view, as placed on B1 rows 48-50
Pin letters per the ALPS SKQUCAA010 data sheet
that Adafruit links as 'similar'. Not on a 0.1"
grid (3.25 mm): bend the legs to snap it in.
VERIFY each direction with a meter to pin 4.
D1, D2 flyback: band (K) to +5V, i.e. B2 bottom half (g13, g42).
D3 opto protection: band (K) in j26 (opto pin 1), stand upright.
4-band code (+ gold); 1% parts have 5 bands - measure
Before fitting, look at the back of the board:
• J1 and J2 must be CLOSED for I2C. Older 938s ship in SPI mode
(bridge both with solder). The current STEMMA QT version ships
• Address: in I2C mode the DC pin is SA0. The firmware only probes
0x3C; Adafruit's 128x64 examples use 0x3D. W27 ties DC to GND
to force 0x3C. Confirm with an I2C scan if it isn't detected.
• Rst: R5 10k to 3V3 + C2 100nF to GND (power-on reset).
Harmless on the newer board, which resets itself.
• Power: Vin ← 3V3. The '3v3' pin is the on-board regulator
OUTPUT: leave it open. CS: leave open in I2C mode.
• Module pull-ups on SDA/SCL are fitted; if yours has none add
4.7k from each to 3V3. SSD1306 is the firmware default.
VCC → V+ (Vin), SCL/SCK → CK, SDA/MOSI → SI,
RES/RST → RT, DC/RS → DC, CS → TC, BLK/BL → BL.
SO (MISO) and CC (SD-card CS) are not used.
Header order above follows the Adafruit guide's pin list.
Check it against the silkscreen; if it differs, keep each
wire on the strip under the matching label.
Detection: firmware probes the OLED at 0x3C first and uses
the TFT only if nothing answers. Both may stay fitted; to
run the TFT, pull W25 (OLED Vin) or build -DMIDIUM_DISPLAY=2.
A1 · Pico 2 pins used + Debug Probe
Debug Probe 'D' port → SWD header at the
far end of the Pico (opposite USB):
yellow SD → SWDIO. Use the JST-to-JST cable
The probe does not supply VBUS: keep the Pico
USB plugged in or the relays never pull in.
Leave the 'U' port unconnected: UART0 is MIDI.
